newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia govt, oppn propose joint race stand.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia govt, oppn propose joint race stand.

text.p: The Australian government and opposition said on Wednesday they had agreed to move a joint motion denouncing racial intolerance in any form.

The motion reaffirms Australia's commitment to the right of all Australians to enjoy equal rights and be treated with equal respect regardless of race, colour, creed or religion, they said in a joint statement.
It also reaffirms Australia's commitment to a non-discriminatory immigration policy and to the reconciliation process with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people.
The motion reaffirms Australia's commitment to maintaining Australia as a culturally diverse, tolerant and open society.
"(The motion) denounces racial intolerance in any form as incompatible with the kind of society we are and want to be," they said.

The joint motion would be moved in the lower house of parliament, the House of Representatives, after question time on Wednesday. The motion was agreed on after discussions between lower house government leader Peter Reith and deputy opposition leader Gareth Evans.
Earlier in October, opposition leader Kim Beazley called for a unified response to racial intolerance towards aborigines and migrants through a bipartisan motion.
The government declined to support the motion as it stood, suggesting instead that opposition and government representatives meet to form an acceptable joint motion.
The new motion removes the opposition's proposal for all members to provide leadership on the racism issue and to present the case for a tolerant, multicultural Australian community.

Australian Prime Minister John Howard has been criticised for not making a stronger stand on racism, after the issue flared in the wake of a controversial speech from independent parliamentarian Pauline Hanson.
Foreign Affairs Minister Alexander Downer warned earlier on Wednesday that Australia's international standing could be damaged by continued publicity for Hanson and the race debate.
